summary: Describes link macros in module docs: R() for cross-references to RST anchors, L() for titled links, U() for bare URLs, M() for module names (FQCN required), and P() for plugin names since ansible-core 2.15.
questions: How do I link to another module from my module's documentation?
What's the difference between L() and U() in Ansible docs?
Why does my M() link come out broken?
How do I refer to a lookup or filter plugin in documentation?
How should I refer to a set of modules spread across collections?

answer_card.title: Link macros in module docs
answer_card.answer_md:
- `R(text,anchor)` cross-reference to an RST anchor (2.10+); use for collection groups too.
- `L(text,URL)` titled link; don't use for relative links between Ansible and collection docs.
- `U(URL)` bare URL.
- `M(fqcn)` module name, e.g. `M(ansible.builtin.yum)`. **FQCNs are required**; short names produce broken links.
- `P(fqcn#type)` plugin name (2.15+), e.g. `P(community.general.json_query#filter)`.
- When a collection isn't the right granularity, use `C(win_*)`.
- Use full URLs for links outside your collection when `R()` isn't available.
